input_oneliner: 78M BPH admitted for CAP, on diphenhydramine qhs, no urine output x8h per RN, Cr up 0.5 overnight

optional_context.objective: no urine output for 8 hours, creatinine up 0.5

reference_targets_freetext.item: Bladder percussion/palpation for retention (suprapubic dullness, palpable mass, tenderness)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Acute urinary retention is the first reversible cause of anuria in an elderly man with BPH on an anticholinergic

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): anticholinergics, opioids, and alpha-agonists; ask about last void, straining, and dribbling
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Diphenhydramine and opioids precipitate retention; the history of small frequent voids or dribbling supports overflow

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vital signs (supine to standing at 1 and 3 min)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Postural tachycardia and dizziness are the most specific bedside findings for hypovolemia in a febrile patient with poor intake

reference_targets_freetext.item: JVP and dry axilla / mucous membranes
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Low JVP and dry axilla support prerenal physiology; high JVP argues against it

reference_targets_freetext.item: Digital rectal examination (DRE) - prostate size and tenderness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Prostate enlargement or prostatitis supports obstruction; tenderness raises prostatitis as the infection source

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about flank pain and hematuria; costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness bilaterally
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Upper tract obstruction or pyelonephritis as alternative causes

off_bedside_acceptable: Foley catheter placement if retention confirmed
should_not_recommend: Fluid bolus for low urine output before bladder exam
Furosemide for oliguria before bladder exam and volume assessment
